small_guidance:
- The current kernel recomputes the conv 4× per output pixel (once per pooling position) — fuse this by computing conv on a contiguous (BLOCK_SP_H × PK, BLOCK_SP_W × PK) tile once and reducing PK×PK into one output. This reuses neighboring input loads and weights across the pool window.
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_OC (e.g. 64/128) paired with smaller BLOCK_SP (e.g. 16) and num_warps=4, plus configs that tile spatial in 2D (BLOCK_PH × BLOCK_PW) instead of flat 1D so KH/KW gathers share input rows across SP lanes.
- Cache the weight tile `w[oc, ic, kh, kw]` outside the IC loop (load once into registers per (kh,kw)) and load `x` with 2D tile indexing so adjacent `ow` lanes share data — currently each (kh,kw,ic) reloads x across the whole BLOCK_SP without spatial locality benefit.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an im2col-style GEMM per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile of post-pool size): K dimension = IC*KH*KW, M = BLOCK_OC, N = BLOCK_SP, accumulate via `tl.dot`. Compute conv at all PK*PK pre-pool positions inside the tile, apply (x - sub1, tanh, - sub2), then sum/PK² in registers before storing. Use channels-last layout so the IC loop is the contiguous GEMM-K axis.
- Alternatively, do a single conv-tile producing a (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_PH*PK, BLOCK_PW*PK) accumulator via `tl.dot` over IC, fuse tanh+subtract in the epilogue, then perform a register-level 2×2 (PK=2) average reduction before storing — this eliminates the 4× redundant input/weight loads in the current scalar-multiply implementation.
- Pre-pack weights at init into [OC, IC*KH*KW] (or a swizzled layout matching the tile), and store on the module so forward avoids per-call `.contiguous()`/`.cuda()` of weight/bias.
